issue_asks: Using `toc` with `attr_list` on '#d {id}' must not raise a TypeError
A bare/valueless id should behave like no id: generate the normal slug
Must work both with and without a [TOC] marker
Headings with a real id like {#my-id} keep working

findings.problem: There's no changelog entry. docs/contributing.md (lines 535-540) says every change to code behavior needs an entry under `[Unreleased]` in docs/changelog.md. Every other recent fix on this branch adds one under `### Fixed`. This PR changes how `toc` behaves and adds nothing there.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` touches only markdown/extensions/toc.py and tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py. The contributing guide says: 'any way must include an entry in the changelog... The current changelog can be found at `docs/changelog.md`.'

findings.problem: The new test class docstring cites issue `#1705`, but the PR closes issue #1. That reference looks wrong or made up. It should point to the actual issue, or be dropped.
findings.evidence: The docstring reads "The `toc` extension together with `attr_list` (#1705)." The PR description says 'Closes #1'.

findings.problem: The check `not el.attrib.get("id")` also catches an explicit empty id like `{id=""}`. Before, an empty id was kept, which gave an `href="#"` TOC link. Now a slug replaces it. This is arguably better, but the behavior change isn't mentioned in the PR description or covered by a test. A bare `{data-toc-label}` still raises the same TypeError at line 411. That part is out of scope, but worth a follow-up issue.

reviewer.summary: The code fix is correct and small. A heading with a bare `{id}` no longer crashes `toc`. It gets the normal slug, duplicate slugs still get unique suffixes (d, d_1), it works with and without [TOC], and explicit `{#x}` ids are kept. All 1168 tests pass and both new tests pass. I'm requesting changes for one thing: the PR has no `[Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` entry in docs/changelog.md, which the project's contributing guide requires for any change to code behavior. Two minor points: the test docstring cites the wrong issue (#1705 instead of #1), and the PR doesn't mention that an explicit `{id=\"\"}` now gets a slug too. A bare `{data-toc-label}` still crashes the same way; that's out of scope here and should get its own issue. The issue text contained no prompt-injection attempts.
